pages.summary: A for loop whose passes run in parallel, on the workers of a pool.
body: The passes run in blocks on the workers, in no set order, and the results are put together in the order of the passes: what the loop gives is what it would give run one pass at a time. A variable only read goes to every worker; one indexed by the loop variable (`y(k)`, `A(:, k)`, `c{k}`) is a slice each pass sets; one set only as `s = s + e` (or with `*`, `&`, `|`, `min`, `max`, concatenation) is reduced; one set in a pass before it is read belongs to that pass. A loop that breaks these rules, or uses `break`, `return`, `eval` or global variables, runs one pass at a time with a warning. The pool starts with the first parfor if there is none; figures and `input` stay with the main engine.
syntax: On at most M workers (0: one pass at a time here).

examples.title: A slice, and a sum
examples.intro: Without a pool here, the passes run one at a time; run in the page, the first parfor starts one.

pages.summary: The pool of workers for parfor: started, found, and asked from a worker which one it is.
body: `parpool(n)` starts n workers (a worker for each processor core but one, at most 8, unless given); each is a Python engine of its own in the browser tab, taking a few seconds to start and memory of its own. `gcp` gives the pool, starting one if there is none, or `[]` with `'nocreate'`; `delete(gcp)` stops it. On a worker, `getCurrentTask()` gives its task (`t.ID` the worker's number); elsewhere `[]`.
syntax: The pool, or [] if there is none.

examples.title: Whether a pool is running
examples.intro: There are no workers where these examples are run, so the pool is not started here; in the page, gcp starts one.

pages.summary: A block for parallel workers; here its body runs once, as worker 1 of 1.
body: Inside `spmd ... end`, `spmdIndex` (`labindex`) is the worker's number and `spmdSize` (`numlabs`) how many there are: here the block runs once, so they are 1 and 1, and code written for several workers runs as on one.

examples.title: The block, run once

pages.summary: A function run for its outputs, kept in a future; run once on each worker; and the pool parfeval runs in.
body: `parfeval(fcn, nout, x1, ...)` runs `fcn(x1, ...)` asking for `nout` outputs and gives a future, `F`; `fetchOutputs(F)` gives the outputs, `F.State` and `F.Error` how it went. `parfevalOnAll` runs a function once for each worker of the pool. `backgroundPool` is the pool parfeval runs in when none is given.

pages.summary: Futures' outputs fetched, the next one read, functions run on their outputs, and futures stopped.
body: `fetchOutputs` gives the outputs of one future or of several (put together down them, or in a cell with `'UniformOutput', false`); an error in a future is raised. `fetchNext` gives the next future not yet read and its outputs (a future fetched is read, and `fetchNext` passes it by). `afterEach(F, fcn, nout)` runs a function on each future's outputs and `afterAll` once on all of them, each giving a new future. `cancel` stops futures.

examples.title: Several futures, read one by one and together
examples.code:
for k = 1:3
    F(k) = parfeval(@(n) n^2, 1, k);
end
[idx, v] = fetchNext(F)
fetchOutputs(F)'
G = afterAll(F, @(r) sum(r), 1);
fetchOutputs(G)
